comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C9-C14. Both evaluations accept the foundational data showing α-SNAP depletion blocks SOCE across multiple cell types with rescue experiments. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of evidence; peer reviewers acknowledge this as an important finding without questioning the data.

Perfect agreement on claims C15-C24. Both evaluations accept the binding and co-localization data demonstrating α-SNAP interactions with Stim1 and Orai1. OpenEval finds the data convergent and sufficient; peer reviewers accept the interactions as important but request additional mechanistic details about functional consequences.

Strong agreement on claims C5, C6, C70, C71 regarding the overarching conclusion about α-SNAP's role in SOCE. Both evaluations accept the core finding and NSF independence. OpenEval integrates multiple results; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as 'a potentially important step' and accept the 'surprising finding' about NSF independence.

Strong agreement on NSF-independence (claims C29-C33, C36, C93, C95). Both evaluations accept the data showing NSF inhibition doesn't affect SOCE and that L294A mutant rescues function. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple lines of evidence; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge NSF-independence as a 'surprising finding' that is established.

Agreement on claims C34-C35 regarding L294A mutant binding to Stim1 and Orai1. OpenEval considers this part of the NSF-independence evidence; peer reviewers specifically requested this data and it was answered by existing manuscript data (Figure 3I-J).

Disagreement on cluster stoichiometry mechanism (claims C7, C55-C57, C61-C62, C72, C83). OpenEval finds the TIRF microscopy and bidirectional manipulation data sufficient to support the stoichiometry hypothesis. Peer reviewers accept that α-SNAP affects cluster composition but find the mechanistic explanation insufficient, explicitly stating 'the data does not reveal how α-SNAP controls the size of the clusters' and requesting additional biochemical experiments.

Agreement on claims C58-C60, C87 regarding α-SNAP's regulation of Orai1:Stim1 ratio. Both evaluations accept the overexpression and depletion data showing bidirectional effects on cluster ratios and SOCE. Peer reviewers acknowledge this ratio regulation as part of the overall finding about cluster composition control.

Disagreement on CAD-mediated SOCE mechanism (claims C52-C54, C84). OpenEval considers the CAD rescue experiment definitive for placing α-SNAP in the activation sequence. Peer reviewers find this observation insufficient and propose a specific mechanistic hypothesis about CC1 inhibition relief, requesting additional recombinant protein binding experiments to test this mechanism.

Disagreement on domain mapping sufficiency (claims C48-C50). OpenEval finds the in vitro binding assays sufficient to map interaction domains. Peer reviewers note 'it is not clear which parts of α-SNAP are required for the interaction with Orai1 and Stim1' and request additional mechanistic experiments beyond the binding data alone.

Disagreement on N-terminal domain characterization (claims C40-C42). OpenEval finds the domain mapping showing N-terminal necessity sufficient. Peer reviewers request clarification: 'can the N-terminal half of α-SNAP...rescue SOCE as well? This would also help to address whether the entire functional domain is contained in the N-terminal fragment.'

Disagreement on LOOP mutant interpretation (claims C45-C47). OpenEval finds the dissociation between SNARE function and SOCE with the LOOP mutant compelling structure-function evidence. Peer reviewers want differential binding analysis: 'the α SNAP LOOP mutant might affect selectively binding to either Stim1 or Orai1, which is important to test.'

OpenEval evaluated background/context claims (C1-C4, C25, C63-C69) as supported established facts with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are not novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluated prior literature claims (C73, C75-C79, C88-C89) as accurately representing published work with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these provide context rather than novel findings.

OpenEval marked speculative/novelty claims (C74, C85-C86, C91) as uncertain, noting they involve mechanistic speculation not directly tested or claims about novelty difficult to verify comprehensively. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these interpretive claims.
